newsitem.title: UK: National Grid confirms cost cut targets.
newsitem.headline: National Grid confirms cost cut targets.

text.p: British electricity transmission business National Grid Group Plc confirmed on Tuesday it should achieve cost cuts of six percent a year in real terms to offset profit losses from new price controls.

The company said annual pretax profits were 591.4 million pounds ($966.5 million), within expectations and up 12.2 percent from pro forma previous results. National Grid paid out a total dividend of 11.13 pence per share.

"We have made rapid progress on rationalising transmission which will enable us to cut controllable costs aggressively and offset...the effects of the new price control," the company said in a statement with results.
It added that it should achieve real growth in dividend per share of "between four and five percent per year" over the next four years.
National Grid said its telecommunications subsidiary Energis turnover increased by 127 percent and loss before interest, tax and depreciation was cut by 66 percent.
The company, demerged from the regional electricity companies (Recs) in December, 1995, agreed to price cuts including a one-off 20 percent decrease this year with regulator Offer last October.
